description: API-shape experiment for a drum step sequencer. The same six tasks are given with no API (desire mode) or with one variant's type declarations only (guess mode). Expectations are variant-agnostic: they describe behaviour, not names.

tasks.prompt: Build a four-lane drum loop (kick, snare, closed hat, open hat) as a 16-step pattern at 120 BPM that loops forever: kick on steps 1, 5, 9, 13; snare on 5 and 13; closed hat on every odd step; open hat on step 15. Use synthesized or loaded sounds, whichever the API makes easiest. Start playback from a button click (browser autoplay rules apply).
expectations: Creates or resumes the audio context inside the click handler (or calls an API documented as doing so).
Defines a 16-step pattern with four lanes whose on-steps match the request (1-based steps 1,5,9,13 / 5,13 / odd / 15, translated correctly if the API is 0-based).
Sets the tempo to 120 BPM.
Playback loops indefinitely (set explicitly, or by the API's documented default).
Each lane is connected to a sound source and the result reaches the speakers.

tasks.prompt: Take a 16-step closed-hat lane and give it accented dynamics: full velocity on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 40% velocity on all other steps. Then add 30% swing to the hat lane only, so every second sixteenth is pushed late.
expectations: Sets per-step velocity: 1.0 (or the API's maximum) on the four accented steps and 0.4 of maximum on the others.
Applies swing to the hat lane only, not globally.
The swing amount corresponds to 30% (0.3 or an equivalent unit).
Does not implement swing by hand-shifting timestamps if the API offers swing.

tasks.prompt: Two things must start in sync: a separately scheduled audio clip that starts at audioContext.currentTime + 0.5, and the step sequencer. Make beat 1 of the sequencer land exactly at that same audio time.
expectations: Computes one target audio time (currentTime + 0.5) and uses it for both the clip and the sequencer.
Starts the sequencer so that its first step sounds exactly at the target time (not 'now' plus a delay measured in JS timers).
Uses audio-clock time, not setTimeout/Date/performance.now, for the alignment.

tasks.prompt: Each step of a bass-drum lane should also carry a filter cutoff in Hz (range 200–8000, default 1200). When a step plays, a low-pass filter on that lane must be set to that step's cutoff exactly when the hit sounds. Set step 1 to 400 Hz and step 9 to 6000 Hz.
expectations: Declares a per-step numeric value for cutoff with the given range and default (or the API's equivalent declaration).
Sets step 1 to 400 and step 9 to 6000 (index translated correctly).
Has a low-pass filter for that lane between its sound and the output.
Applies the cutoff at the hit's scheduled audio time (e.g. setValueAtTime(value, when)), not immediately when the callback runs.

checks.label: step 1 -> 400 and step 9 -> 6000 at the variant's index

tasks.prompt: Add humanization to all lanes: each hit is moved by a random amount of up to ±8 milliseconds, and its velocity varies by up to ±10%. The randomness must be reproducible from a seed, and editing the pattern must not re-randomize hits that are already scheduled.
expectations: Adds a timing offset bounded by ±8 ms (0.008 s) per hit.
Adds a velocity variation bounded by ±10% and keeps velocity in the valid range.
Randomness is derived from a seed (a seeded generator or a per-hit stable hash), not Math.random.
The per-hit randomness is stable for the same hit (e.g. keyed by lane/step/loop), so re-scheduling does not change it.
Uses the API's extension point for modifying hits if one exists, rather than reimplementing scheduling.

tasks.prompt: While the sequencer is playing, turn snare step 7 on with velocity 0.8 so it is heard the next time step 7 comes round, without stopping playback. Later, stop playback and release every audio resource the sequencer created, with no sound continuing afterwards.
expectations: Edits the single cell (lane snare, step 7, velocity 0.8; index translated correctly) through the API while playing.
Does not stop/restart playback to make the edit take effect (or relies on an API that re-queues automatically (explicitly or by its documented default), or calls the API's documented refresh).
Stops playback so that no further hits sound.
Releases/disposes the resources the sequencer created (nodes, timers, subscriptions) via the API's teardown.

checks.label: snare step 7 -> velocity 0.8 at the variant's index
